notes: Writer-aware Linux persistence file-write rules. Each rule pairs a file.path regex with a per-path legit-writer allowlist; the same allowlist doubles as a PARENT-basename gate so dpkg/apt/rpm maintainer scripts (which run the write as an sh/dash child of the package manager) are suppressed - this resolves the dpkg-maintainer-script FP that refuted the source rules. config_mgmt_suppressed drops NAMED agents only (ansible/puppet/chef/salt/cloud-init) - bare python3 is intentionally NOT suppressed to avoid a malware blind spot. abuse_markers escalate severity (staging-dir writer / shell-web parent); require_to_fire promotes them to a fire gate for the marked rules. content_regex is SIEM-side/documentation only - the agent matcher (Test-PersistenceWrite) has no file-content or command_line field. tightened_from_review=true marks rules whose fix_suggestion was applied before shipping. DROPPED: persist_shellinit_user_dotfile (~/.bashrc) - its only discriminator is appended content, unavailable in this data model, so it cannot ship at fidelity.

name: [Loaded Potato] Runtime Linker Preload Write (/etc/ld.so.preload)
description: Creation or modification of /etc/ld.so.preload, the global list of libraries the dynamic linker force-loads into every dynamically linked process at startup - the canonical userland-rootkit persistence and function-hooking vector. Always fires: the file does not exist on a default install and no mainstream package edits it, so its mere creation is the persistence act.
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: always_fire: an ld.so.preload write is essentially never legit; abuse_markers only escalate. Residual (intended) FP: a handful of legit global-preload libs (libeatmydata, snoopy, jemalloc/tcmalloc swaps, some EDR/observability sensors) configure themselves here - rare deployment-time-only events worth one-time verification. content_regex is SIEM-side only (the agent matcher has no file-content/command_line field).
benign_scenarios: libeatmydata / snoopy command logger / jemalloc-tcmalloc allocator swap installing a system-wide preload
EDR or observability sensor (CrowdStrike/Sysdig/Aqua) configuring process injection via ld.so.preload

name: [Loaded Potato] Cron Fragment Write by Non-Package Writer (/etc/cron.*)
description: A file created or changed under /etc/crontab or /etc/cron.{d,daily,hourly,weekly,monthly}/ by a writer that is neither a cron/package tool nor a package-manager child. Tightened per review: the parent-basename gate suppresses dpkg/apt maintainer scripts (which run the write as an sh/dash child of dpkg).
query: file.path: (\/etc\/cron.d\/* or \/etc\/cron.daily\/* or \/etc\/cron.hourly\/* or \/etc\/cron.weekly\/* or \/etc\/cron.monthly\/* or \/etc\/crontab) and not process.name: (dpkg or dpkg-deb or apt or apt-get or rpm or yum or dnf or zypper or crontab or run-parts)
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Fires on non-allowlisted writers to system cron dirs. dpkg/rpm maintainer scripts write as an sh/dash child of the package manager - resolved by the parent-basename gate (parent in legit_writers => suppress). Residual FP: an admin authoring a fragment with vim (writer=vim) fires; accepted (worth one-time review). content_regex is SIEM-side only.
benign_scenarios: Package maintainer script generating /etc/cron.d/<pkg> (writer sh/dash, parent dpkg) - suppressed by parent gate
Admin editing a cron fragment in an editor - fires, accepted residual

name: [Loaded Potato] User Cron Spool Direct Write (/var/spool/cron)
description: A direct write to a user cron spool file (/var/spool/cron/<user> or /var/spool/cron/crontabs/<user>) that bypasses crontab(1). Tightened per review: requires an abuse marker to fire (staging-dir writer or shell/web parent), which drops control-panel (Webmin/cPanel perl/php daemons) and backup/restore writers that run from normal paths under non-shell parents; the at-spool dirs are excluded from the path.
query: file.path: (\/var\/spool\/cron\/* or \/var\/spool\/cron\/crontabs\/*) and not process.name: (crontab or cron or crond or cronie or dpkg or apt)
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: require_to_fire keeps the python/tee-from-/tmp malware case while dropping panel/backup/config-mgmt daemons (normal path, non-shell parent => no marker => suppressed). atjobs/atspool dirs excluded from path_regex so the `at` package dir-creation does not trip it. Parent gate suppresses dpkg maintainer scripts.
benign_scenarios: Webmin/cPanel/Plesk provisioning writing the spool as a perl/php daemon (no shell parent, normal path) - suppressed (no abuse marker)
`at` package creating /var/spool/cron/atjobs - excluded by path_regex

name: [Loaded Potato] Systemd System Unit Write by Non-Package Writer
description: A .service/.timer/.socket/.path/.mount unit file created under /etc/systemd/system or /usr/lib/systemd/system by a non-package, non-systemctl writer. Tightened per review: parent gate suppresses dpkg/rpm maintainer scripts, config-mgmt suppression drops named agents, and an abuse marker is required to fire so a clean unit from a normal path does not alert.
query: file.path: (\/etc\/systemd\/system\/* or \/usr\/lib\/systemd\/system\/* or \/lib\/systemd\/system\/*) and (file.path: *.service or file.path: *.timer or file.path: *.socket) and not process.name: (dpkg or dpkg-deb or apt or rpm or dnf or yum or zypper or systemctl or systemd or deb-systemd-helper)
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Units SHIPPED in a .deb are written by dpkg itself (allowlisted); units GENERATED in a postinst run as an sh/dash child of dpkg and are caught by the parent gate. require_to_fire (staging-dir writer OR shell/web parent) removes admin/config-mgmt noise; the parent-package-manager gate takes precedence over the parent_is_shell marker so a maintainer wrapper is never escalated. [^/]+ excludes .wants/ enable-symlinks and .d/ drop-in overrides. content_regex (ExecStart pointing at /tmp,curl,...) is SIEM-side only.
benign_scenarios: dpkg unpacking a shipped unit (writer dpkg) - allowlisted
postinst generating a unit (writer sh, parent dpkg) - suppressed by parent gate
Ansible/Salt writing a unit as a named agent - config-mgmt suppressed

name: [Loaded Potato] Systemd User Unit Write by Non-Package Writer
description: A user-scope systemd unit written directly under ~/.config/systemd/user/ by a non-allowlisted writer. Tightened per review: config-mgmt suppression (Ansible/home-manager/cloud-init as named agents) plus a required abuse marker, since a bare interpreter writing a user unit is otherwise indistinguishable from provisioning.
query: file.path: \/.config\/systemd\/user\/* and (file.path: *.service or file.path: *.timer or file.path: *.socket) and not process.name: (systemctl or systemd)
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Package maintainer scripts install SYSTEM units, never a user ~/.config/systemd/user, so dpkg is not the dominant benign writer here; config-management is. require_to_fire + config_mgmt suppression drop Ansible/home-manager/cloud-init. Residual/uncovered: agentless Ansible running as bare python3 with no agent parent cannot be distinguished by process name and may FP. content_regex is SIEM-side only.
benign_scenarios: home-manager/Nix activation symlinking a user unit as a named agent - config-mgmt suppressed
Ansible template of a user unit via a named ansible process - suppressed

name: [Loaded Potato] Dynamic Linker Search-Path Write (/etc/ld.so.conf*)
description: A write to /etc/ld.so.conf or /etc/ld.so.conf.d/*.conf, which inject a directory into the dynamic linker library search path (library-hijack persistence). Tightened per review: parent gate suppresses package post-install scriptlets (Oracle/Intel driver .rpm/.deb writing ld.so.conf.d as an sh child of rpm/dpkg) and an abuse marker is required.
query: file.path: (\/etc\/ld.so.conf or \/etc\/ld.so.conf.d\/*) and not process.name: (dpkg or rpm or dnf or yum or zypper or ldconfig or update-alternatives)
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: path_regex end-anchors on ld.so.conf / ld.so.conf.d/*.conf and deliberately excludes ld.so.cache and ld.so.preload. Post-install scriptlets write as sh/dash children of the package manager - caught by the parent gate. require_to_fire (staging-dir writer OR shell/web parent) removes the routine driver/library-install noise (content points at /opt, not a staging dir). content_regex is SIEM-side only.
benign_scenarios: Intel MKL / Oracle Instant Client .rpm %post writing /etc/ld.so.conf.d/*.conf (writer sh, parent rpm) - suppressed by parent gate

name: [Loaded Potato] Account Database Write (/etc/passwd) by Non-Account Tool
description: A write to /etc/passwd by a process that is not a standard account-management or package tool. Tightened per review: the allowlist now includes update-passwd/chpasswd/vipw/systemd-sysusers/busybox (routine provisioning/patching writers), the parent gate covers debconf-wrapped maintainer scripts, and an abuse marker is required to fire.
query: file.path: \/etc\/passwd and not process.name: (useradd or usermod or userdel or adduser or deluser or passwd or chpasswd or newusers or vipw or update-passwd or systemd-sysusers or dpkg or apt or rpm)
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: base-passwd postinst runs update-passwd (now allowlisted); chpasswd/newusers are allowlisted for cloud-init/ansible/container builds. require_to_fire keeps the echo/tee/sed >>/etc/passwd vector (shell parent or /tmp writer) while dropping package-tool noise. content_regex (:0:0: UID-0 row) is SIEM-side only and, per review, does not evaluate against a piped tee/sed argv - do not rely on it agent-side.
benign_scenarios: base-passwd upgrade running update-passwd - allowlisted
cloud-init/ansible chpasswd batch set - allowlisted
postinst echo>>/etc/passwd as sh child of dpkg - suppressed by parent gate

name: [Loaded Potato] Shadow Hash Write (/etc/shadow) by Non-PAM Non-Account Tool
description: A write (create/change, including nshadow-rename) to /etc/shadow or /etc/gshadow by a process outside the account-management, package, and PAM-session sets. Tightened per review: PAM login writers (sshd/login/gdm/su/sudo) are allowlisted so a forced-password-change at login does not fire, and MITRE is corrected from T1003.008 (a READ/dump technique) to write/modify-auth techniques.
query: file.path: (\/etc\/shadow or \/etc\/gshadow) and not process.name: (passwd or chpasswd or newusers or chage or useradd or usermod or userdel or vipw or pwck or sshd or login or su or sudo or dpkg or apt or rpm)
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: MITRE corrected: this detects credential INJECTION/write, not dumping - T1556.003 / T1098 / T1136.001 (not T1003.008, which is the READ technique covered separately by Module 5c). PAM writes /etc/shadow in-process as sshd/login/gdm/su/sudo during a forced password change - these are allowlisted so a routine expired-password login does not fire. require_to_fire (staging-dir writer OR shell/web parent) keeps the printf>>/etc/shadow appliance-postinst and python-writing-a-$6$-hash cases while suppressing PAM/pwck. content_regex ($1/$5/$6/$y prefix) is SIEM-side only.
benign_scenarios: Expired-password forced change at login (writer sshd/login/gdm, in-process) - allowlisted
pwck -s repair in maintenance cron - allowlisted

name: [Loaded Potato] Sudoers Write by Non-Sudo-Tool Writer
description: A write to /etc/sudoers or /etc/sudoers.d/* by a writer other than visudo/cloud-init (or a package/config-mgmt process). Tightened per review: the parent gate reaches through dpkg maintainer scripts (agent packages dropping a sudoers.d fragment as an sh child of dpkg), config-mgmt suppression drops Ansible/Puppet/Chef, and an abuse marker is required so the NOPASSWD content marker no longer escalates every fleet run to CRITICAL.
query: file.path: (\/etc\/sudoers or \/etc\/sudoers.d\/*) and not process.name: (visudo or cloud-init or dpkg or apt or rpm or dnf or yum or zypper)
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: zabbix/nagios/datadog etc. drop /etc/sudoers.d/<pkg> from a postinst run as an sh child of dpkg - caught by the parent gate. Ansible/Puppet/Chef fragments run as named agents - config-mgmt suppressed. require_to_fire keeps the /tmp-dropper and shell-parent NOPASSWD writes; the acknowledged admin-vim case still fires only when the write comes from a shell/staging context. content_regex (NOPASSWD) is SIEM-side only.
benign_scenarios: Monitoring-agent postinst dropping /etc/sudoers.d/<pkg> (writer sh, parent dpkg) - suppressed by parent gate
Ansible sudo fragment via a named agent - config-mgmt suppressed

name: [Loaded Potato] PAM Configuration Write (/etc/pam.d) by Non-PAM-Tool Writer
description: A write under /etc/pam.d/ by a writer that is not a PAM/package tool. Tightened per review: dpkg/dpkg-deb (direct .deb unpack of a shipped PAM file - the single most common pam.d write) and pam-auth-update/authselect are allowlisted, and the parent gate suppresses the wrapper-shell maintainer case.
query: file.path: \/etc\/pam.d\/* and not process.name: (pam-auth-update or authconfig or authselect or dpkg or dpkg-deb or apt or rpm or dnf or yum or zypper)
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Direct-unpack writes are attributed to dpkg/dpkg-deb itself (allowlisted). A maintainer script that edits pam.d as a shell BUILTIN (echo>) appears as writer=sh with parent=dpkg and is caught by the parent gate. Documented residual/uncovered: a maintainer script using a SEPARATE process (sed -i/install) gives writer=sed, parent=sh, grandparent=dpkg - the auditd model exposes only one parent level, so this two-level wrapper is not suppressed and may FP. require_to_fire is off (a shell-parent gate would misfire on that same maintainer sed); abuse markers escalate only.
benign_scenarios: apt install openssh-server: dpkg creates /etc/pam.d/sshd - allowlisted
pam-auth-update rewriting common-auth - allowlisted

name: [Loaded Potato] SSH authorized_keys Write by Non-Provisioning Writer
description: A write to any ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (or authorized_keys2) by a writer outside the provisioning/allowlist set. Tightened per review: provisioning agents (cloud-init/vmtoolsd/qemu-guest-agent/amazon-ssm-agent/nova-agent) are allowlisted, the dead content_regex is dropped (auditd carries no file content), and CRITICAL escalation is restricted to a staging-dir writer - a shell parent alone no longer auto-escalates (that trait is shared by ssh-copy-id, interactive admins, and agentless Ansible).
query: file.path: \/.ssh\/authorized_keys* and not process.name: (cloud-init or vmtoolsd or qemu-guest-agent or amazon-ssm-agent or nova-agent or ssh-copy-id)
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Base fires HIGH on any non-provisioning authorized_keys write (worth one-time review). CRITICAL only when the writer executes from a staging dir (/tmp,/dev/shm,...) - parent_is_shell_or_web is deliberately DISABLED as an escalator here because sshd-spawned sh is the parent for legit ssh-copy-id AND interactive admins. Documented residual/uncovered: agentless Ansible (writer python3 under sshd->sh, no ansible process on the node) and ssh-copy-id (writer = login shell) both fire HIGH - they cannot be distinguished from an interactive key add by process name alone.
benign_scenarios: cloud-init injecting the instance key at first boot - allowlisted
Agentless Ansible authorized_key module as python3 (no ansible parent) - fires HIGH, documented residual

name: [Loaded Potato] SSHD Config Write by Non-Package Writer
description: A write to /etc/ssh/sshd_config or /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf by a non-package writer. Tightened per review: the parent gate + ucf/cloud-init/crypto-policies allowlisting suppress the dpkg-postinst / ucf-conffile-merge / config-mgmt writers that the original rule (and its own example_negative) false-positived on; content_regex is corrected to flag only PermitRootLogin yes (not the hardened prohibit-password default).
query: file.path: (\/etc\/ssh\/sshd_config or \/etc\/ssh\/sshd_config.d\/*) and not process.name: (dpkg or apt or rpm or dnf or ucf or cloud-init or sshd)
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: ucf/conffile merges delegate the replacement to cp/mv run under dpkg - the parent gate (parent in package-manager/ucf set) suppresses them. Ansible/puppet as named agents are config-mgmt suppressed. require_to_fire keeps the /tmp-drop and shell-parent backdoor writes; admin vim edits that just change a Port do not fire. content_regex flags only PermitRootLogin yes / AuthorizedKeysCommand / ForceCommand and is SIEM-side only.
benign_scenarios: dpkg conffile/ucf merge of sshd_config via cp under dpkg - suppressed by parent gate
Ansible managing sshd_config as a named agent - config-mgmt suppressed

name: [Loaded Potato] System Shell-Init Write (/etc/profile*, bash.bashrc) by Non-Package Writer
description: A write to /etc/profile, /etc/profile.d/*.sh|*.csh, or /etc/bash.bashrc by a non-package writer - a system-wide login payload. Tightened per review: the parent gate suppresses dpkg maintainer scripts, config-mgmt suppression drops Ansible/Puppet/Chef/Salt (whose parent_is_shell trait previously made a legit push look MORE malicious), and an abuse marker is required to fire.
query: file.path: (\/etc\/profile or \/etc\/profile.d\/* or \/etc\/bash.bashrc) and not process.name: (dpkg or apt or rpm or dnf or yum or zypper or ucf)
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: require_to_fire (staging-dir writer OR shell/web parent) + parent gate + config-mgmt suppression remove the dpkg-postinst and Ansible/Puppet/Chef writers. Because config-mgmt is filtered BEFORE marker evaluation, the parent_is_shell marker no longer misfires on a legit Ansible push. Residual: an admin one-off /etc/profile.d script authored from a shell fires (medium). Note: the user-dotfile variant (~/.bashrc) was DROPPED from this bundle - its only discriminator is appended-line content, which neither the auditd file-event model nor this matcher can see, so it degenerates to firing on every rustup/nvm/conda dev install. content_regex here is SIEM-side only.
benign_scenarios: Package postinst regenerating /etc/profile.d/*.sh as sh child of dpkg - suppressed by parent gate
Ansible template of /etc/profile.d/company.sh as a named agent - config-mgmt suppressed
